decision: The current backtesting vertical slice implements orchestration through NautilusTrader BacktestNode rather than a Bolt-owned simulator. BacktestNode receives manifest-mapped BacktestRunConfig, BacktestVenueConfig, and BacktestDataConfig values; Bolt-owned code performs validation, provenance binding, result packaging, and claim-limit enforcement around the NT run.

evidence.proof: run_nt_backtest_node maps the BacktestingRunManifest into NT config, constructs BacktestNode, builds the node, attaches an existing compiled Rust strategy to the NT engine, runs BacktestNode, and returns the single NT BacktestResult.

BacktestingRunManifest maps venue settings, one or more catalog inputs, catalog storage options, instrument ids, start/end bounds, TradeTick, and OrderBookDelta into NT BacktestVenueConfig, BacktestDataConfig, and BacktestRunConfig. Unsupported NT catalog-query and complex venue surfaces are rejected before config construction.
Catalog fixtures write/query NT-native instruments and data, then run BacktestNode over NT OrderBookDelta and TradeTick inputs with iteration-count assertions.
The end-to-end slice validates accepted source proof, canonical projection, NT catalog read-back, BacktestNode execution, and objective result-contract construction.

The one-off binary-option L2 path writes selected-source rows into NT ParquetDataCatalog, runs BacktestNode over verified OrderBookDelta catalog input, and binds the result contract to conversion and selector provenance.

non_hardcoding_boundary: The orchestration layer is selected by manifest/catalog/data-class configuration and uses NT config APIs. Source-specific conversion remains isolated to raw-source-to-NT-typed projection modules and must not become venue/provider branching inside BacktestNode orchestration.
